method: Static source and control-flow review; Base64/zlib and custom JavaScript string-table recovery; original sources traced with external effects stubbed.

trait_changes.consumers: Exact references follow all nine observations. Former requests and HTTP-library directory selectors retain GET membership. Response-acquisition selector retains GitHub client co-occurrence. The Python-only Discord consumer retains its effective webhook endpoint; its invite alternative never admitted Python.
unsupported_claims_corrected: An aliased import is a declaration, not a data operation.
One litellm_params token does not identify the containing program as the LiteLLM library.
requests.get is an HTTP GET operation, independent of client library.
A raw-GitHub URL and a Python HTTP client can co-occur without proving that URL was requested or a file was saved.
trait_changes.deliberate_membership_change: A lone LiteLLM parameter token no longer activates blanket library exclusions. The collector gains an accurate encoded HTTP URL finding.

verification.focused_fixture_result: All observations and dependent findings identical after ID mapping; controls scanned outside testdata to exercise URL rules.
verification.shared_rule_result: No finding or severity changes after ID mapping, including original Ultralytics malware fixture, SQLi/webshell consumers, local backups, overwritten HTTP bodies, and wheel members.
verification.python_traces: No live network, database, file, fork or remote-payload execution. See python-trace.json.

samples.marker_contents: Video player: origin-checked media bridge; keep obfuscation traits
behavior_evidence: Custom Base64 alphabet; checksum rotation is 43 positions. Replacing decoded string lookups recovers all application behavior.
Accepts only an 11-character YouTube ID or 5-12-digit Vimeo ID. Builds a provider iframe with a fixed trusted origin.
Checks both message source and origin. Parent messages target the fixed loopback origin using the current port. YouTube commands are allowlisted; Vimeo maps commands to playback or volume methods.

CSP restricts frames to the two providers and disables other default resource sources and form actions. No credential harvesting, arbitrary code dispatch, external callback, or destructive path is present.
samples.missing_context: Parent application and original distribution are unknown; no product attribution is asserted.

samples.marker_contents: LiteLLM collector: concealed secret export; correct trait placement
behavior_evidence: At module scope, imports aliased zlib/base64, decompresses the embedded source and executes it without a main-entry guard.
Decoded code connects Prisma and queries credential_name/credential_values from LiteLLM_CredentialsTable and model_name/litellm_params from LiteLLM_ProxyModelTable, up to 500 records each.

The exact query results enter the JSON body of a cleartext POST to http://www.litellm.dev/healthcheck. A healthcheck does not require exporting provider secrets; this and concealed automatic execution tip the verdict.
Database queries and packing can serve legitimate uses independently; their accurate suspicious findings remain, and local backups retain collection coverage without export detection.
samples.missing_context: No enclosing wheel, installation path, database configuration or consent context was supplied. Live exfiltration success and actor attribution are not asserted.

samples.marker_contents: Python startup backdoor: hourly remote exec; correct HTTP traits
behavior_evidence: When imported as sitecustomize, main obtains a nonblocking exclusive lock on /tmp/remote_code_loader.lock, forks, detaches via setsid, changes to / and redirects descriptors 0, 1 and 2 to /dev/null.
The child fetches a GitHub raw domain list. It accepts the first hostname/optional-port line matching the regex and fetches http://<resolved-host>/codepy.
The returned source reaches exec through the bound helper functions. The loader suppresses BaseException and repeats on a 3600-second interval.
The Python startup hook plus detached, silent, unauthenticated recurring remote-code execution provides persistent backdoor access; it is not ordinary Python environment customization.
samples.missing_context: Actual installation into a Python import path, operator authorization and the remote payload are unavailable. No final-stage stealing or other payload behavior is invented.

remaining_disagreements: ML continues to flag the benign video player; accurate obfuscation detection is retained.
coverage_gap: cook.py has one distinct hostile source-to-send export, plus three suspicious collection/concealment findings. Another hostile finding would duplicate the theft or overstate dual-use querying/packing.
